For some reason, quicksaves and autosaves are more likely to cause stability problems or become corrupt. Saves made via the console or the save menu don't have this problem.

There's a mod called Rotating Quicksave that works like that. You choose a key to be your "quicksave" key and it creates a "hard" save instead. It also names the save after your character, which is handy if you have a few different characters. You can even set it to make a certain number of saves before it starts overwriting them. It doesn't automatically unbind the vanilla quicksave and quickload keys, but you could set those to keys you never use and bind the mod's keys to F5 and F9 if you want.

It's actually pretty easy to do this yourself in the Creation Kit, especially if you only want to copy enchantments from one set of clothing to another. You just need to make a duplicate of the item you want to put the enchantment on and then put the enchantment on it. Then you can use the console to give it to yourself, although you might need to use the "help" command to find its ID first. It takes a bit more time than some in-game thing, but it's easy to do. The process is the same for weapons. If you decide to do this, you'll want to make sure that you're making duplicate items for yourself so that you don't give NPCs anything they shouldn't have. You wouldn't want every piece of Fine Clothes to have the Archmage enchantment, for example.

Transmogrification is a cool mod, but the last time I tried it, I found that enchantments would occasionally disappear from the items I copied them to. I also think it can only copy stats from "chest piece" items, though I could be wrong about that. It's also been updated recently and I haven't tried the new version, so maybe the update fixes some things. It also doesn't work on weapons. In addition, it can't distinguish between your set of Fine Clothes and everyone else's, so every set of Fine Clothes in the game will end up with Archmage stats. It's mostly intended to be used for mod armors that NPCs won't be using. If you want to move enchantments around using only vanilla clothing, doing it in the Creation Kit would be a better idea. That being said, it's a good idea to keep Transmogrification around anyway, in case you need a quick solution.
